video_title_guess: No Fouls Given: Paul Pierce, Danny Green, Big Wos

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: What we saw was a team that was satisfied with beating Boston after coming down from 3-1 and laid an egg versus New York. And it just shows that New York is a far superior team. The Knicks, I mean the Philly, I can't trust them with Embiid. Embiid, I don't know if he's going to. Embiid actually said he sees this season as a success, him personally. Well, yeah, that's Philly. They have low expectations there. If someone from Boston would have said that, nobody would ever say that. So Philly doesn't have the same expectations as Boston because they were picked to lose and then they won, then they got swept. So if that's your leadership and if that's your expectations and if that's your ceiling in Philly, then go ahead and do that because we don't do that in the franchises I play for.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce criticizes Joel Embiid's statement about the 76ers' season being a success, implying a lack of championship ambition compared to franchises he played for.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.quote: I got to give a lot of credit to the Knicks. I think Philly fought. Game 3 was bad. The Knicks came out historically great. I was wrong about them too. I didn't think, I said coming out of the end of the season, they didn't look consistent. They looked up and down, they looked shaky. OG is out. I thought Philly would get at least two games. But they are playing the best basketball in the playoffs as of right now to me, even with OKC. They're playing the best basketball. They're getting production from Shamet, they're getting production from Deuce. Deuce hit 4 threes in like 3 minutes. And that's when it was crazy.
quotes.why_it_matters: Danny Green acknowledges his misjudgment of the Knicks' playoff potential, praising their consistent and historically great performance, especially given injuries.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.quote: I wouldn't say this season was a success for them. They over-exceeded certain people's expectations, but beginning of the year, being a last year with those three guys, they were supposed to make noise. Same with this year, as healthy, they're supposed to. First time seeing healthy, they're supposed to make noise. You end up being a 7 seed. You beat a 2 seed, so that's over-exceeding, but being a 7 seed, I think is kind of not meeting. That's a disappointing. And then losing after you beat the 2 seed, you lose in the second round like that. Now, I don't mind you losing, but you should lose in a better fashion. But again, I got to give a lot of credit to the Knicks because they're playing unbelievable basketball right now. They're playing championship, like they're a championship team right now. If they keep playing like that, they will have Larry O'Brien in their comfort of their home.
quotes.why_it_matters: Danny Green critiques the 76ers' season as a disappointment, arguing that despite beating a higher seed, their overall performance and second-round exit fell short of expectations for a healthy roster.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: Dinosaurs would have to come back to Earth. We're going to see Jesus walk down Crenshaw. Like, come on, the Knicks aren't winning nothing, bro. They do this every. You guys know, listen, this is not me trolling because it's not. New York does this every year. They get everybody all excited and then, we're going to win it, parade in the streets. And they're going to do something that's going to disappoint everyone. They do it every year. I promise you, I've seen this for the last 25 years. So they're going to lose to Detroit in the next round. They're definitely going to lose to Detroit. Or they're going to go up 3-0 in the Finals and lose four straight. It's going to be something devastating. We all know this.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce dismisses the Knicks' championship aspirations with humor, citing a historical pattern of New York teams building hype only to disappoint their fans in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: I think that the Knicks are a bad matchup for Detroit. Detroit dominated them this year in the regular season, if I'm not mistaken. I'm just going off memory, I'm not going off no computer, but I think Detroit beat them by an average of like 20 points. They put belt to ass on the Knicks. So what is giving me any kind of optimism that the Knicks can do it now, especially if OG Anunoby, who's a key contributor for the Knicks, who's averaging 21 points a game, being out versus the Detroit Pistons who not only have Cade Cunningham, who in my eyes could have easily won the MVP. They haven't announced MVP yet, but he definitely is a top 3 player in the NBA. And Detroit, the way they're playing now defensively, and I know they lost the last game because James Harden woke up out of his grave and decided he wanted to play playoff basketball and contributed. But I truly believe Detroit is going to be Detroit versus OKC. So you're betting people?
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce predicts the Pistons will defeat the Knicks, citing Detroit's regular season dominance over New York, the absence of OG Anunoby, and Cade Cunningham's MVP-caliber play.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.quote: I got the Knicks. I think they're a bad matchup for either one of those teams, especially the way they're playing right now. Again, I said, if, if they keep playing like this. Now, at any moment, they could have moments where they implode. Danny's a Knicks skeptic as well, guys. I'm just again, my whole life, I've seen them too. I've watched them. I've watched them do some things that are disappointing. Even last year, like, oh, we got it, you know, we beat Boston, now we got Indiana, we could get them. I'm like, all right, and they thought they had them. Don't count your eggs before they hatch. But they are playing really good basketball right now. And I think Detroit, Cleveland, I'm not confident in either one of those groups in the playoffs. Now, Detroit in the regular season, look phenomenal. In the playoffs, they look better.
quotes.why_it_matters: Danny Green expresses cautious optimism for the Knicks, believing they are a tough matchup for their next opponent if they maintain their current level of play, despite his historical skepticism about their playoff consistency.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: How are you confident in the Knicks in the playoffs? Because they just smacked Atlanta crazy. Because they're playing. Because they've done it before. They look great. They look like the best team. Philly beat your Boston team and they just beat. Detroit looks great. Detroit does not look great. But I'm happy you have that opinion. I will just say, unlike my esteemed colleagues on the panel, I picked the Knicks to go to the Finals before the playoffs started. By the way, everybody, he's from New York. That has nothing to do with it. Of course, of course he picked the Knicks to go to the Finals. Of course. Because, you know what, me being a Celtic, it's just that my whole life, being a Celtic, I got to deal with the most delusional fans on Earth. They are. So, the Knicks. These are the three most delusional fans on planet Earth: Knicks fans, Lakers fans, Dallas Cowboys fans. The three most delusional fans on planet Earth.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce vehemently dismisses the Knicks' playoff chances, labeling their fanbase as 'delusional' and comparing them to other teams with historically inflated expectations.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: When Wembanyama got kicked out of the game for what was clearly a flagrant 2, I heard you saying for the love of the playoffs, they should keep him in the game. But bro, he literally attacked a man. He bugged out. He bugged out. He did not attack a man. What happened there? Explain to the people what that play was. In my day, that's just an offensive foul, we move on. Today, everybody's so soft that you kick, you kick everybody out of the game and, oh, you should be in jail for that elbow. Get that out of here, bro. He didn't attack him. So you would have preferred a flagrant 1? Flagrant 1, let's play on. Let's play our best versus your best. Let's not let the refs dictate the series. Let's, all right, here, give them some free throws, move on. Let them play.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce argues that Wembanyama's flagrant foul should have been a lesser penalty, emphasizing that referees should not dictate playoff series by ejecting star players for incidents that would have been considered minor in previous eras.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.quote: What I disagree with about that is if any player on the Timberwolves, maybe maybe excluding Ant, but probably not. Any player did that to Wemby, they don't even look at the monitor. He's just out. They just kick him out of the game straight up. That's not proven. He doesn't have that aura yet. That's not proven. But now that Wemby has done it, it's given if they give that leeway to do it, now somebody else has the leeway to do it as well. That's the standard now. So now somebody could elbow Wemby in his neck or throat. He's like the most impossible player to elbow. His face is way up there. Well, that's fair. I guess you got to do it to his knee or something. Like, yeah, his face is way up there. How can you elbow? That was just a frustration get off me type of foul. That ain't like, I don't think he was trying to knock somebody out. I don't know, man. I just think he was like, get off me. He looked the guy square in his eye. He couldn't see him. Winded up. And then just boom. He looked him square in his eye is crazy. He almost killed. No, it's a miracle he finished the game. I liked it. It's a miracle he finished the game. He looked him square in his eye is crazy.
quotes.why_it_matters: The panel debates the double standard of Wembanyama's flagrant foul, suggesting that if another player had committed the same act against him, they would have been ejected without review, setting a dangerous precedent.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: The most impressive thing for me for San Antonio is how young these guys are playing like veterans. Because usually when you got a team that's one of the best, you don't really play a lot of rookies. Dillon Harper and the other kid over there for San Antonio, what's his name? Carter Bryant. They're in the rotation as rookies and you don't see that a lot from a contending team. Rookies are usually inconsistent and they don't understand the moments, especially when you get later in the playoffs. But this kid Dillon Harper, I mean, you can tell he's way ahead of his years. Of course, his daddy Ron Harper who played for the Lakers, won a championship, played for the Bulls, won a championship there, played Spurs in different places. You could tell that his daddy really gave him the knowledge and he he he's cut from a certain cloth and that that's impressive to me that what they're able to do. San Antonio rookies, especially Dillon Harper, the way he contributes. It's just like he fits right in and comes off the bench. He should be starting probably on 99% of the NBA teams, but he's playing a great job. This is the thing about rookies. When you're a rookie in the NBA, you're not even thinking about winning a championship. You know what you're thinking about? You're thinking about establishing yourself, making a name for yourself. You want people to know who you are and then you like, I'm trying to build up my stock to get a big contract. As a rookie, because you made it, now you're trying to prove yourself. But when you're a rookie and you fall in line and you play a certain role on a championship team, that that's that's maturity right there. He's very mature.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce highlights the impressive maturity of Spurs rookies Dillon Harper and Carter Bryant, noting their ability to contribute effectively on a contending team, which is rare for young players focused on personal contracts.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.quote: For the Laker fans in the house, if the Lakers had Luka in this series, would this have gone differently? Yeah, you really think so? I don't. I really do think if they're scoring 131 without Luka, one of the worst defenders I've ever seen, it's going 150. Well, listen, they're losing by an average of 20, right? Yeah. Luka averages 34. Yeah. Do the math. So, the Lakers would be winning every game by 14. They would give. I'm saying, I'm just saying, I don't know. Let's do the math. I think they would get one game. It's, come on. They're coming to the series without their MVP candidate. You can't expect them to beat the world champions. We said if he's there. Yeah, if Luka was there, they would get one game. Sure. I could have seen this going. But it's still, this is the NBA champions. They weren't, it was going to be an uphill battle regardless if Luka was there or not. I don't know if they could, they had enough because it's not just the stars that are doing stuff for OKC. They're doing this without J-Dub. Chet is playing incredibly. Isaiah Joe one game, then it's Jalen McCan another game, then it's Cason Wallace. You still got Alex Caruso. They got a lot of guys, they got AJ Mitchell, he's playing like a veteran point guard. He's a second, third year guard. Getting 24 and 10. They have a lot of guys, a lot of weapons that are stepping up.
quotes.why_it_matters: The panel debates whether Luka Doncic's presence would have altered the Lakers' playoff series against OKC, with Wosny Lambre arguing that OKC's depth and overall team performance would still make it an uphill battle for the Lakers.

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.quote: I'm in practice and stuff. So Wesley Johnson cooking me. And so I'm like, hold on. Wesley Johnson not supposed to be cooking me. And then, you know, we coming out like after the second week of practice. Doc like, you're not starting. I was like, what? This is really my first time ever not starting my whole career. I've played 17 years. I've been a starter my whole life. They're like, all right, we're going to bring you off the bench. I was like, all right, you know what? It must be over for me. I got to start looking. It must be over. So then I was like getting to practice every day early. So practice starts at 11:00, so I'm going to get there at like 8:00 AM. And I'm telling all the rookies and second years, y'all be here at 8:00 AM because I'm going to put y'all through a workout, you know, get y'all ready. We're going to lift, run, get some shots up. And that's where it all just kept in my mind. I was like, you know what, you you're a coach now with a player contract. 17 years is a hell of a run, bro. Starting for 17 years is crazy. I'm going to show all these young boys how to be a pro. And so this is my way, like, here, y'all got to get here, be like, y'all want to be a pro as long time, this is what you got to do. And I was like, all right, and I had to come to grips with that. I had to come, it was hard. It's hard. When you've been one way your whole life. I've been a starter since I was six years old. I'm not a starter no more. Like, what the hell am I supposed to do? So I just had to come to that reality, like, all right, it's time for me to help out the young boys. I'm on my way out, so I'm going to give them some game. Look, this is how you got to prepare. This is how you got to be every day. And I was happy with that. And, uh, but yeah, once Wesley Johnson started cooking me. Yeah, you're 18. Wesley Johnson was the one on that James Harden take that got crossed over and he fell. And James Harden told him to get up. I got cooked by him. I knew it was over.
quotes.why_it_matters: Paul Pierce recounts the moment he realized his NBA career as a starter was over, attributing it to being outplayed by Wesley Johnson and subsequently being moved to the bench, which led him to embrace a mentorship role for younger players.
